Tessa (ILLUSTRATIVE) borrows $320,000 in the week of October 8, 2026: a 15-year mortgage at 6.73%, or a 30-year at 7.40% paid off in 15 years anyway, keeping the 30-year's lower required payment, about $613 a month lower, as a fallback for a bad month. Paying the 30-year in 15 years takes $2,948 a month against the 15-year's $2,828: $120 a month, $21,622 over 15 years. That is the stack, the price of the fallback.

We replayed 1,833 weeks of the Freddie Mac weekly mortgage survey, from August 1991 to the week of October 8, 2026, and priced the same plan in every week. The stack ranged from $6,097 to $29,502, with a typical week at $16,631; fewer than 1 in 5 weeks cost as much as the week of October 8, 2026. Paying the 30-year exactly what the 15-year costs ends about 15 months late; finishing in 180 months takes $733 a month on top of the required payment. The same extra sent as $8,792 once a year ends in 184 months and charges about $8,200 more in interest.

Then the bar: each extra dollar of principal on Tessa's 30-year saves interest at exactly the loan rate, 7.40% a year, before taxes. That is interest no longer charged, not an investment return. Leo (ILLUSTRATIVE), who borrowed in January 2021 at 2.65%, shows the same plan in a different week: a stack of $13,231 ($74 a month) and a fallback of about $793 a month.

**Chủ dự án quyết 11/10:** thumbnail API lai **KHÔNG ĐẠT** — không dùng, không render đối chứng 2D; bộ nhận diện `tongket-t6/thumbs/api-*.png` (logo "M.", chữ dưới trái, màu theo trụ) **không duyệt**. **Gói phát hành (tiêu đề, mô tả, thumbnail, tag) do chủ dự án làm trên ChatGPT.** Claude cung cấp đầu vào và kiểm đầu ra.
